- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: lines 99-111 (REDACTION_PATTERNS), 157-160 (redact), 451 (report), 483 (_occurrence_block) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The PR newly passes the matched allow rule through `redact()` and publishes it — in `report()` JSON printed to stdout (line 451) and in the GitHub issue/comment occurrence block (line 483). However, `redact()`'s credential pattern at line 106 requires an `=` or `:` separator after the keyword: `(?i)\b(token|secret|password|passwd|api[_-]?key)(\s*[=:]\s*)[^\s'\"]+`. A space-delimited option value like `--password plainsecret` or `--api-key mykey` is NOT matched, so the credential survives redaction and is published to GitHub.
  WHY: An allow rule such as `Bash(curl --password plainsecret *)` in `.claude/settings.json` would match a denied `curl --password plainsecret ...` command. `redact()` leaves `plainsecret` unchanged because there is no `=` or `:` after `password`. The redacted rule is then printed by `report()` to the session stdout and posted to a public GitHub issue via `_occurrence_block`. The existing test `test_report_redacts_the_matched_rule` only covers the `Bearer` form (caught by a separate pattern at line 105), so the gap is untested.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
